statement: The Australian Museum's public Pukumani account quotes Tiwi artist Pedro Wonaeamirri and describes commemorative funerary ceremonies centered on carved tutini posts, songs and dance; it also states that contemporary practices can include Christian elements.

sources.citation: Australian Museum, 'Burial — Pukumani, Tiwi Islands', paragraphs after Pedro Wonaeamirri's statement, updated 6 Dec 2018, https://australian.museum/about/history/exhibitions/death-the-last-taboo/burial-pukumani-tiwi-islands/
sources.author: Australian Museum with Tiwi quotation from Pedro Wonaeamirri
sources.access_note: Public page read, including attributed Tiwi testimony, description of ceremonies, tutini posts and acknowledged Christian elements. Does not reproduce sacred restricted instructions.

does_not_demonstrate: Ceremonial accounts do not establish an archaeological date for the origins of Pukumani.
Christian elements cannot be projected backward unchanged into pre-contact practice.
A short museum introduction does not exhaust local ceremonial variants or community authority.
adversarial_counter: Museum curation provides a limited external context; source-community custodianship and consent govern further detail.
notes: Institutional-source audit. Scope: named public page and its content only; no tradition founding-year inference. Independent historical / community review required before status change.
